brief description: A common skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become clogged with oil and dead skin cells.
causes: Hormonal changes, excess sebum production, bacteria (Propionibacterium acnes), and genetics.
symptoms: Whiteheads, blackheads, pimples, oily skin, and scarring.
treatment: Topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, salicylic acid, antibiotics. For severe cases, oral isotretinoin may be prescribed.
dosage: Children: Topical medications (e.g., benzoyl peroxide 2.5-5%) applied once daily. Adults: Same topical treatments; oral antibiotics (e.g., doxycycline 100mg twice daily) or isotretinoin (0.5-1mg/kg/day) for severe cases.

brief description: Inflammation of the nasal passages caused by an allergic reaction to airborne substances.
causes: Exposure to allergens such as pollen, dust mites, pet dander, or mold.
symptoms: Sneezing, runny nose, itchy nose/eyes/throat, watery eyes, and nasal congestion.
treatment: Avoidance of allergens, antihistamines, nasal corticosteroids, and decongestants.
dosage: Children: Cetirizine syrup (5mg/5ml) 2.5-5ml once daily for ages 2-6; 10ml for ages 6+. Adults: Cetirizine 10mg once daily; Fluticasone nasal spray 2 sprays per nostril once daily.

brief description: A progressive neurodegenerative disease that causes brain cells to waste away and die, leading to dementia.
causes: Unknown, but linked to genetic mutations, age, and the accumulation of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles in the brain.
symptoms: Memory loss, confusion, difficulty with thinking and reasoning, disorientation, changes in personality and behavior.
treatment: Cholinesterase inhibitors, NMDA receptor antagonists, and supportive care to manage symptoms.
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: Donepezil 5-10mg once daily; Memantine 5-20mg once or twice daily; dosage adjusted based on kidney function.

brief description: A mental health condition characterized by excessive and persistent worry, fear, and nervousness.
causes: Genetics, brain chemistry, personality, and traumatic life events.
symptoms: Restlessness, increased heart rate, rapid breathing, sweating, trembling, difficulty concentrating, and sleep problems.
treatment: Psychotherapy (CBT), antidepressant medications (SSRIs, SNRIs), and anti-anxiety medications.
dosage: Children: SSRIs like Sertraline (25-50mg once daily) for ages 6+; dosage based on weight. Adults: Sertraline 50-200mg once daily.

brief description: A chronic respiratory condition that involves inflammation and narrowing of the airways, causing breathing difficulties.
causes: Genetics, allergies, respiratory infections, and environmental triggers like smoke or pollution.
symptoms: Wheezing, shortness of breath, chest tightness, and coughing, especially at night or early morning.
treatment: Inhaled corticosteroids (preventers), bronchodilators (relievers), and leukotriene modifiers. [citation:5]
dosage: Children: Inhaled Fluticasone (88 mcg) 2 puffs twice daily; Albuterol (90 mcg) 1-2 puffs every 4-6 hours for symptoms. Adults: Fluticasone (250 mcg) 2 puffs twice daily; Albuterol (90 mcg) 2 puffs every 4-6 hours.

brief description: A common fungal infection of the skin on the feet.
causes: Fungus (Trichophyton) that thrives in warm, moist environments like shoes and public showers.
symptoms: Itchy, scaly rash between the toes; burning or stinging; cracked, peeling skin; blisters.
treatment: Over-the-counter or prescription antifungal creams, powders, or sprays.
dosage: Children: Terbinafine cream (1%) applied 1-2 times daily for 1-2 weeks. Adults: Same as children; oral Terbinafine (250mg once daily) for 2-6 weeks if topical treatment fails.

brief description: An irregular and often very fast heart rhythm (arrhythmia) that can lead to blood clots in the heart.
causes: High blood pressure, heart disease, alcohol abuse, hyperthyroidism, and heart surgery.
symptoms: Palpitations, shortness of breath, fatigue, dizziness, chest pain, and weakness.
treatment: Medications to control heart rate/rhythm, blood thinners to prevent stroke, and sometimes cardioversion or ablation.
dosage: Children: Digoxin (10 mcg/kg/day) for rate control; dosage adjusted by serum levels. Adults: Metoprolol 25-100mg twice daily; Apixaban 5mg twice daily (reduced for age/renal function).

brief description: Inflammation of the bronchial tubes, often caused by a viral infection, leading to excessive mucus production.
causes: Viral infections, bacterial infections, and exposure to tobacco smoke or air pollution.
symptoms: Persistent cough with clear, yellow, or green mucus; shortness of breath; wheezing; chest tightness; fatigue; fever. [citation:5]
treatment: Rest, fluids, cough suppressants, and sometimes bronchodilators or antibiotics (if bacterial). [citation:5]
dosage: Children: Albuterol syrup (2mg/5ml) 0.1-0.15mg/kg 3-4 times daily. Adults: Albuterol inhaler (90 mcg) 2 puffs every 4-6 hours; Doxycycline 100mg twice daily for 7 days (if bacterial).

brief description: Clouding of the eye's natural lens, which leads to a decrease in vision.
causes: Aging, diabetes, smoking, excessive alcohol use, and prolonged exposure to UV sunlight.
symptoms: Blurred, cloudy vision; difficulty seeing at night; sensitivity to light and glare; seeing halos; fading of colors.
treatment: Surgery to remove the cloudy lens and replace it with an artificial one.
dosage: Children: Not applicable (surgical). Adults: Not applicable (surgical).

brief description: A mild viral infection of the upper respiratory tract.
causes: Numerous viruses, most commonly rhinoviruses.
symptoms: Runny/stuffy nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, headache, mild fatigue, and low-grade fever.
treatment: Rest, fluids, over-the-counter decongestants, antihistamines, and pain relievers.
dosage: Children (6-12 years): Pseudoephedrine (30mg) 1 tablet every 4-6 hours. Adults: Pseudoephedrine (60mg) 1 tablet every 4-6 hours. Paracetamol based on weight for fever. [citation:6]

brief description: Infrequent and difficult bowel movements.
causes: Diet low in fiber, dehydration, lack of exercise, certain medications, and medical conditions.
symptoms: Fewer than 3 bowel movements a week, hard/dry/lumpy stool, straining, and feeling of incomplete evacuation.
treatment: Increase fiber and water intake, exercise, and use of laxatives or stool softeners.
dosage: Children (2-6 years): Polyethylene Glycol 3350 (1/4 capful) in water once daily. Adults: Polyethylene Glycol 3350 (1 capful) in water once daily.

brief description: A chronic inflammatory lung disease that causes obstructed airflow from the lungs.
causes: Long-term exposure to irritating gases or particulate matter, most often from cigarette smoke. [citation:5]
symptoms: Shortness of breath, wheezing, chest tightness, chronic cough, and frequent respiratory infections. [citation:5]
treatment: Smoking cessation, bronchodilators, inhaled corticosteroids, pulmonary rehabilitation, and oxygen therapy. [citation:5]
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled once daily; Fluticasone/Salmeterol 250/50 mcg 1 puff twice daily.

brief description: A urinary tract infection (UTI) that affects the bladder, commonly caused by E. coli.
causes: Bacteria entering the urethra and bladder, sexual activity, and improper wiping technique.
symptoms: Frequent urge to urinate, burning with urination, cloudy or strong-smelling urine, pelvic pain, and lower abdominal pressure.
treatment: Antibiotics to kill the bacteria and pain relievers to ease symptoms. [citation:2]
dosage: Children: Amoxicillin-clavulanate (20-40mg/kg/day of amoxicillin) divided into 2-3 doses for 7 days. Adults: Nitrofurantoin (100mg) twice daily for 5 days.

brief description: A blood clot that forms in a deep vein, usually in the leg.
causes: Prolonged immobility, surgery, injury, cancer, obesity, smoking, and certain genetic disorders.
symptoms: Leg pain, swelling, redness, warmth, and tenderness in the affected area.
treatment: Blood thinners (anticoagulants) to prevent clots from growing or breaking loose.
dosage: Children: Enoxaparin (1mg/kg) injected subcutaneously twice daily; dosage based on weight. Adults: Enoxaparin (1mg/kg) twice daily or Warfarin (5mg daily) adjusted to INR of 2-3.

brief description: A common and serious medical illness that negatively affects how you feel, the way you think, and how you act.
causes: Genetics, brain chemistry, stress, trauma, and major life changes.
symptoms: Persistent sadness, loss of interest, changes in appetite or sleep, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and thoughts of death or suicide.
treatment: Psychotherapy, antidepressant medications (SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics), and brain stimulation therapies.
dosage: Children (adolescents): Fluoxetine (10-20mg once daily) for ages 8+. Adults: Fluoxetine 20-80mg once daily.

brief description: An autoimmune condition where the pancreas produces little to no insulin.
causes: Autoimmune reaction destroying insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas; genetics and environmental triggers.
symptoms: Increased thirst/frequent urination, extreme hunger, unintended weight loss, fatigue, blurred vision, and slow-healing sores.
treatment: Insulin therapy (multiple daily injections or pump), blood sugar monitoring, and dietary management.
dosage: Children: Insulin glargine (0.2-0.4 units/kg) once daily plus rapid-acting insulin (Novolog) with meals (based on carbohydrate intake). Adults: Same principles; total daily insulin 0.5-1 unit/kg.

brief description: A chronic condition that affects the way the body processes blood sugar (glucose).
causes: Genetics, obesity, physical inactivity, age, and insulin resistance.
symptoms: Increased thirst/frequent urination, hunger, fatigue, blurred vision, slow-healing sores, and tingling/numbness in hands/feet.
treatment: Lifestyle changes (diet and exercise), oral medications, and sometimes insulin.
dosage: Children (10+): Metformin (500mg) twice daily. Adults: Metformin (500mg) twice daily; dosage can be increased to 1000mg twice daily. [citation:8]

brief description: Infection or inflammation of pouches (diverticula) that can form in the digestive tract.
causes: A diet low in fiber, leading to increased pressure in the colon, causing pouches to bulge out and become inflamed.
symptoms: Abdominal pain (often left lower quadrant), fever, nausea, vomiting, constipation, and diarrhea.
treatment: Mild cases: diet modification and antibiotics. Severe cases: hospital care, IV antibiotics, or surgery.
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: Ciprofloxacin (500mg) twice daily and Metronidazole (500mg) 3 times daily for 7-10 days.

brief description: A condition that makes skin red, inflamed, and itchy, often seen in people with allergies or asthma.
causes: Genetics, immune system dysfunction, and environmental triggers like dry skin, irritants, and stress.
symptoms: Dry, itchy skin; red to brownish-gray patches; small raised bumps; thickened, cracked, or scaly skin.
treatment: Moisturizers, corticosteroid creams, and antihistamines for itching.
dosage: Children: Hydrocortisone cream (1%) applied to affected area twice daily. Adults: Betamethasone valerate (0.1%) cream applied twice daily for 2-4 weeks.

brief description: A disorder in which tissue similar to the tissue that normally lines the uterus grows outside the uterus.
causes: Unknown, but involves hormonal and immune system factors.
symptoms: Painful periods, pain during intercourse, pain with bowel movements, and infertility.
treatment: Pain relievers, hormone therapy (birth control, progestins), and surgery (laparoscopy).
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: Oral contraceptives (e.g., Norethindrone 5mg 2-3 times daily) or GnRH agonists (e.g., Leuprolide 3.75mg monthly IM).

brief description: A central nervous system disorder in which brain activity becomes abnormal, causing seizures.
causes: Genetics, head trauma, brain tumors, stroke, and infections.
symptoms: Recurrent seizures (generalized tonic-clonic, absence, myoclonic), temporary confusion, staring spells, and jerking movements.
treatment: Anticonvulsant medications, surgery, or dietary therapy (ketogenic diet).
dosage: Children: Levetiracetam (10-20mg/kg) twice daily; dosage adjusted for weight. Adults: Levetiracetam (500-1500mg) twice daily.

brief description: A condition characterized by widespread musculoskeletal pain accompanied by fatigue and sleep issues.
causes: Unknown, but likely involves abnormal pain processing in the brain and spinal cord; genetics and infections may be triggers.
symptoms: Widespread pain, fatigue, cognitive difficulties ("fibro fog"), headaches, depression, and sleep disturbances.
treatment: Pain relievers, antidepressants, anticonvulsants, and lifestyle modifications like exercise and stress reduction.
dosage: Children: Pregabalin (75mg) twice daily for ages 12+. Adults: Pregabalin (75-150mg) twice daily; Duloxetine (30-60mg) once daily.

brief description: A temporary increase in body temperature, often due to an illness or infection.
causes: Infections, heat exhaustion, inflammatory conditions, medications, and autoimmune conditions.
symptoms: Elevated body temperature >37°C, chills, sweating, headache, weakness, and loss of appetite. [citation:2][citation:9]
treatment: Treating the underlying cause, rest, fluids, and antipyretics (e.g., Paracetamol, Ibuprofen). [citation:2]
dosage: Children: Paracetamol 15mg/kg every 4-6 hours (max 75mg/kg/day). [citation:6] Adults: Paracetamol 500-1000mg every 4-6 hours (max 4g/day). [citation:6]

brief description: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines, commonly called the stomach flu.
causes: Virus (rotavirus, norovirus), bacteria (Salmonella), parasites, food allergies, and toxins. [citation:2][citation:9]
symptoms: Diarrhea, vomiting, stomach pain/cramps, nausea, fever, and chills. [citation:2][citation:9]
treatment: Hydration (oral rehydration solution), rest, and symptomatic relief (e.g., antiemetics). [citation:2]
dosage: Children: Oral rehydration solution (ORS) 50-100ml/kg over 4 hours. Adults: ORS as needed; anti-diarrheal Loperamide 4mg initially, then 2mg after each loose stool.

brief description: A group of eye conditions that damage the optic nerve, often linked to elevated pressure in the eye.
causes: Increased intraocular pressure, family history, age, and certain medical conditions.
symptoms: Often no early symptoms. Later: loss of peripheral vision, eye pain, nausea, and halos around lights.
treatment: Prescription eye drops to reduce pressure, laser therapy, or surgery.
dosage: Children (pediatric): Beta-blocker drops (Timolol 0.5%) 1 drop twice daily. Adults: Prostaglandin analog (Latanoprost 0.005%) 1 drop once daily.

brief description: A common form of inflammatory arthritis characterized by sudden, severe attacks of pain in the joints, often the big toe.
causes: High levels of uric acid in the blood, which can form crystals in joints.
symptoms: Sudden severe pain, swelling, redness, and tenderness in the joint, often the big toe.
treatment: NSAIDs, colchicine, corticosteroids, and medications to lower uric acid levels (e.g., allopurinol). [citation:4]
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: Colchicine 1.2mg initially, then 0.6mg after 1 hour (acute); Allopurinol 100-300mg daily (maintenance). [citation:4]

brief description: A partial or total inability to hear.
causes: Aging, noise exposure, infections, genetic factors, birth complications, and earwax buildup.
symptoms: Difficulty hearing, speaking in a louder voice, asking others to repeat themselves, and ringing in the ears (tinnitus).
treatment: Hearing aids, cochlear implants, assistive listening devices, and surgery.
dosage: Children: Not applicable (device). Adults: Not applicable (device).

brief description: A chronic condition where the heart doesn't pump blood as well as it should.
causes: Coronary artery disease, high blood pressure, previous heart attack, diabetes, and heart valve problems.
symptoms: Shortness of breath, fatigue, swelling in the legs/ankles/feet, rapid weight gain from fluid retention, and persistent cough.
treatment: Lifestyle changes, medications (ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, diuretics), and sometimes devices or surgery.
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: Lisinopril (2.5-10mg) once daily; Furosemide (20-40mg) once/twice daily.

brief description: Swollen veins in the lower rectum and anus.
causes: Straining during bowel movements, chronic constipation/diarrhea, sitting for long periods, and pregnancy.
symptoms: Painless bleeding, itching/irritation, swelling, pain, and a lump near the anus.
treatment: Fiber supplements, sitz baths, topical creams, and in severe cases, surgical removal.
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: Topical Hydrocortisone 1% cream applied as needed; rubber band ligation for persistent cases.

brief description: A serious liver infection caused by the hepatitis B virus (HBV).
causes: Contact with infected blood, semen, or other body fluids.
symptoms: Jaundice (yellow skin/eyes), dark urine, severe fatigue, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain.
treatment: Acute: supportive care. Chronic: antiviral medications (e.g., entecavir, tenofovir) and liver monitoring.
dosage: Children: Entecavir (0.015mg/kg) once daily for ages 2+. Adults: Entecavir (0.5mg) once daily.

brief description: The presence of high levels of fat in the blood (hyperlipidemia).
causes: Diet high in saturated fats, inactivity, genetics, and obesity.
symptoms: Often no symptoms. Can cause chest pain if arteries are narrowed by atherosclerosis.
treatment: Lifestyle changes (diet/exercise) and lipid-lowering medications (statins). [citation:8]
dosage: Children (10+): Atorvastatin (10mg) once daily. Adults: Atorvastatin (10-80mg) once daily.

brief description: High blood pressure, a major risk factor for heart disease and stroke.
causes: Obesity, high salt diet, inactivity, smoking, genetics, and stress.
symptoms: Often no symptoms. May cause headaches, shortness of breath, or nosebleeds in severe cases.
treatment: Lifestyle changes (diet/exercise) and blood pressure medications (ACE inhibitors, diuretics, CCBs).
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: Lisinopril (10-40mg) once daily; Hydrochlorothiazide (12.5-25mg) once daily. [citation:8]

brief description: An overactive thyroid gland that produces too much thyroxine.
causes: Graves' disease, toxic nodular goiter, and thyroiditis.
symptoms: Weight loss, rapid heartbeat, nervousness, sweating, tremors, fatigue, and frequent bowel movements. [citation:11]
treatment: Antithyroid medications (Methimazole, Propylthiouracil), beta-blockers for symptom control, or radioactive iodine. [citation:11]
dosage: Children (adolescents): Methimazole (5-10mg) 3 times daily. Adults: Methimazole (5-15mg) 1-3 times daily; Propranolol (10-40mg) 3-4 times daily. [citation:11]

brief description: An underactive thyroid gland that doesn't produce enough thyroxine.
causes: Hashimoto's disease, thyroiditis, or iodine deficiency.
symptoms: Fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, memory problems, and depression.
treatment: Synthetic thyroxine (Levothyroxine) hormone replacement. [citation:7]
dosage: Children: Levothyroxine (mcg/kg) based on age and weight (e.g., 2-4 mcg/kg for 1-3 years). Adults: Levothyroxine (50-200 mcg) once daily. [citation:7]

brief description: A common sleep disorder that makes it hard to fall asleep, stay asleep, or get restful sleep.
causes: Stress, anxiety, depression, poor sleep habits, caffeine, medications, and medical conditions.
symptoms: Difficulty falling asleep, waking up during the night, waking too early, daytime fatigue, and poor concentration.
treatment: Behavioral changes (sleep hygiene, CBT-I), and sometimes sedative-hypnotic medications.
dosage: Children: Not recommended for pharmacologic treatment. Adults: Zolpidem (5-10mg) once nightly for short-term use.

brief description: A common disorder affecting the large intestine.
causes: Unknown; linked to gut-brain axis, abnormal muscle contractions, and bowel inflammation.
symptoms: Abdominal pain, cramping, bloating, gas, diarrhea, and constipation.
treatment: Diet changes (low FODMAP), stress management, and medications for symptom relief.
dosage: Children: Not recommended for pharmacologic treatment. Adults: Dicyclomine (10-20mg) 3-4 times daily; Loperamide for diarrhea.

brief description: Pain in the lower back, often caused by strain, muscle injury, or degenerative conditions.
causes: Muscle or ligament strain, bulging or ruptured discs, arthritis, and osteoporosis.
symptoms: Aching, shooting, or stabbing pain in the lower back; pain that radiates down the leg; limited flexibility.
treatment: Pain relievers, heat/ice, physical therapy, and sometimes surgery.
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: Ibuprofen 400-800mg 3 times daily; Acetaminophen 500-1000mg 4 times daily; muscle relaxants (Cyclobenzaprine 10mg 3 times daily).

brief description: The time that marks the end of a woman's menstrual cycles.
causes: Natural decline in reproductive hormones (estrogen, progesterone) as a woman ages.
symptoms: Irregular periods, hot flashes, night sweats, vaginal dryness, mood swings, and sleep disturbances.
treatment: Lifestyle modifications and hormone replacement therapy (HRT) to manage symptoms.
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: HRT - Estradiol (0.5-1mg) oral daily or transdermal patches.

brief description: A neurological condition often characterized by severe, debilitating headaches.
causes: Genetics, hormonal changes, stress, sensory stimuli, sleep changes, and certain foods.
symptoms: Throbbing head pain, nausea, vomiting, sensitivity to light/sound, and visual disturbances (aura).
treatment: Acute: NSAIDs, triptans. Preventive: Beta-blockers, anticonvulsants, and CGRP inhibitors.
dosage: Children (6+): Sumatriptan nasal spray (5-20mg) for acute attack; Propranolol (1-2mg/kg/day) for prevention. Adults: Sumatriptan (50-100mg) for acute; Propranolol (80-240mg) daily for prevention. [citation:8]

brief description: The most common form of arthritis, causing degeneration of joint cartilage.
causes: Aging, joint injury, obesity, and genetics.
symptoms: Joint pain, stiffness, especially in the morning, tenderness, swelling, and a grating sensation. [citation:4]
treatment: Pain relievers, physical therapy, exercise, and joint replacement surgery if severe. [citation:4]
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: Acetaminophen (325-650mg) every 4-6 hours; NSAIDs (Naproxen 220-440mg) twice daily. [citation:4]

brief description: A bone disease that occurs when the body loses too much bone or makes too little bone.
causes: Aging, hormonal changes (estrogen/testosterone drop), low calcium/vitamin D, and certain medications.
symptoms: Often no symptoms until a fracture occurs (often in hip, spine, wrist). Loss of height and stooped posture.
treatment: Lifestyle changes (diet/exercise) and medications (bisphosphonates) to slow bone loss. [citation:8]
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: Alendronate (70mg) once weekly; Calcium (1000-1200mg) and Vitamin D (800-1000 IU) daily.

brief description: An infection or inflammation of the middle ear, common in children.
causes: Bacteria or viruses entering the middle ear, often following a cold or respiratory infection.
symptoms: Ear pain, difficulty sleeping, tugging at the ear, fever, fluid drainage, and hearing problems.
treatment: Pain relievers, antibiotics (if bacterial), and sometimes ear tubes for recurrent infections.
dosage: Children: Amoxicillin (80-90mg/kg/day) divided into 2 doses for 10 days. Adults: Amoxicillin (500-875mg) twice daily for 7 days.

brief description: Open sores that develop on the inside lining of the stomach and the upper portion of the small intestine.
causes: H. pylori infection, long-term use of NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen), and stomach acid.
symptoms: Burning stomach pain, nausea, bloating, heartburn, and intolerance to fatty foods.
treatment: Antibiotics (for H. pylori), proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), and acid reducers (H2 blockers).
dosage: Children: Omeprazole (0.7-1.4mg/kg) once daily for 2 months. Adults: Omeprazole (20-40mg) once daily; Clarithromycin (500mg) and Amoxicillin (1g) twice daily for H. pylori.

brief description: An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs.
causes: Bacteria (Streptococcus pneumoniae), viruses, and fungi.
symptoms: Cough with phlegm, fever, chills, shortness of breath, chest pain, and fatigue. [citation:5]
treatment: Antibiotics (if bacterial), antiviral medications (if viral), rest, fluids, and oxygen therapy. [citation:5]
dosage: Children: Amoxicillin (90mg/kg/day) divided into 2 doses for 5-7 days. Adults: Azithromycin (500mg) once daily for 3-5 days; Levofloxacin (750mg) once daily for 5 days.

brief description: A skin disease that causes red, itchy, scaly patches.
causes: Immune system dysfunction and genetics.
symptoms: Patches of thick red skin with silvery scales, dry/cracked skin, itching, and thickened nails.
treatment: Topical treatments (steroids, vitamin D analogues), phototherapy, and systemic medications.
dosage: Children: Topical Calcipotriene cream applied 1-2 times daily; low-potency steroids. Adults: Methotrexate (10-25mg) once weekly; Adalimumab (40mg) subcutaneous every 2 weeks.

brief description: A chronic inflammatory disorder that can affect more than just your joints.
causes: Autoimmune system mistakenly attacks body's tissues; genetics and environmental triggers.
symptoms: Tender, warm, swollen joints, joint stiffness (especially mornings), fatigue, fever, and weight loss.
treatment: Disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs), biologics, and physical therapy.
dosage: Children (JIA): Methotrexate (10-15mg/m2) once weekly; Etanercept (0.8mg/kg) weekly. Adults: Methotrexate (15-25mg) once weekly; Hydroxychloroquine (200-400mg) daily.

brief description: A serious mental disorder in which people interpret reality abnormally.
causes: Genetics, brain chemistry, and environmental factors.
symptoms: Delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thinking, abnormal motor behavior, and negative symptoms (lack of emotion).
treatment: Antipsychotic medications and psychosocial therapy.
dosage: Children (adolescents): Aripiprazole (2-5mg) once daily, titrated based on response. Adults: Risperidone (1-6mg) once/twice daily; Clozapine (300-450mg) daily.

brief description: A painful skin rash caused by the varicella-zoster virus (the same virus that causes chickenpox).
causes: Reactivation of the varicella-zoster virus, often due to aging, stress, or immunosuppression.
symptoms: Painful rash with blisters, itching, tingling, fever, headache, and sensitivity to light.
treatment: Antiviral medications (Acyclovir), pain relievers, and cool compresses.
dosage: Children: Not applicable (rare). Adults: Acyclovir (800mg) 5 times daily for 7-10 days; Valacyclovir (1g) 3 times daily for 7 days.

brief description: Inflammation or swelling of the tissue lining the sinuses.
causes: Viral or bacterial infection, allergies, nasal polyps, and a deviated septum.
symptoms: Facial pain, nasal discharge, stuffy nose, headache, cough, fever, and fatigue.
treatment: Nasal decongestants, saline sprays, pain relievers, and antibiotics (if bacterial).
dosage: Children: Amoxicillin (80-90mg/kg/day) divided into 2 doses for 10 days. Adults: Amoxicillin (875mg) twice daily for 10-14 days.

brief description: A medical emergency where blood supply to part of the brain is interrupted or reduced.
causes: High blood pressure, smoking, high cholesterol, diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and heart disease.
symptoms: Sudden numbness/weakness of face/arm/leg (often one side), confusion, trouble speaking, vision problems, and severe headache.
treatment: Immediate emergency care, clot-busting drugs (tPA), and rehabilitation (physical/occupational/speech therapy).
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: Thrombolytics (tPA 0.9mg/kg IV) within 4.5 hours of onset; Aspirin (325mg) within 48 hours.

brief description: A condition in which you lack enough healthy red blood cells to carry adequate oxygen to your body's tissues.
causes: Iron deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency, chronic disease, and genetic disorders (sickle cell, thalassemia).
symptoms: Fatigue, weakness, pale skin, shortness of breath, dizziness, and cold hands/feet.
treatment: Treatment depends on the cause: iron supplements, vitamin B12 supplements, and medications (erythropoietin).
dosage: Children (Iron deficiency): Ferrous sulfate (3-6mg/kg/day) divided into 2-3 doses. Adults: Ferrous sulfate (65mg) 3 times daily.

brief description: Inflammation of the appendix, a small pouch attached to the large intestine.
causes: Blockage of the appendix by stool, a foreign body, or cancer.
symptoms: Sudden pain around the navel or lower right abdomen, nausea, vomiting, fever, and loss of appetite.
treatment: Appendectomy (surgery to remove the appendix).
dosage: Children: Not applicable (surgical). Adults: Not applicable (surgical).

brief description: A mental health condition characterized by extreme mood swings.
causes: Genetics, brain structure, and stressful life events.
symptoms: Extreme highs (mania or hypomania) and lows (depression), irritability, impulsivity, and decreased need for sleep.
treatment: Mood stabilizers (Lithium, anticonvulsants), antipsychotics, and psychotherapy.
dosage: Children (adolescents): Lithium (15-30mg/kg/day) divided into 2-3 doses; dosage adjusted by serum levels (0.6-1.2 mEq/L). Adults: Lithium (900-1800mg/day); Quetiapine (300-600mg/day).

brief description: A highly contagious viral infection causing an itchy, blister-like rash.
causes: Varicella-zoster virus.
symptoms: Itchy rash, fever, tiredness, loss of appetite, and headache.
treatment: Antihistamines for itching, calamine lotion, and sometimes antiviral medications for severe cases.
dosage: Children: Antihistamine (Diphenhydramine) 5mg/kg/day for itching; antiviral Acyclovir not usually needed in healthy children. Adults: Acyclovir (800mg) 4 times daily for 5 days.

brief description: Inflammation of the gallbladder, often caused by gallstones.
causes: Gallstones blocking the cystic duct, leading to bile build-up.
symptoms: Sudden, intense abdominal pain (right upper quadrant), nausea, vomiting, and fever.
treatment: Gallbladder removal surgery (cholecystectomy) for recurrent episodes.
dosage: Children: Not applicable (surgical). Adults: Not applicable (surgical).

brief description: Inflammation or infection of the transparent membrane (conjunctiva) that lines your eyelid.
causes: Virus, bacteria, or allergies. [citation:2][citation:9]
symptoms: Redness, itching, tearing, and a discharge. [citation:2][citation:9]
treatment: Depends on the cause: antiviral, antibiotics, or antihistamine eye drops. [citation:9]
dosage: Children: Antibiotic drops (Polymyxin B/Trimethoprim) 1 drop 4 times daily. Adults: Same; antihistamine drops (Olopatadine) 1 drop twice daily for allergies.

brief description: A genetic disorder that causes severe damage to the lungs, digestive system, and other organs.
causes: Mutations in the CFTR gene, inherited from both parents.
symptoms: Persistent cough, wheezing, frequent lung infections, salty-tasting skin, poor growth, and greasy stools.
treatment: Airway clearance techniques, inhaled medications, pancreatic enzymes, and CFTR modulator therapies.
dosage: Children: Dornase alfa inhaled daily; pancreatic enzymes (lipase 500-2500 units/g fat) with meals. Adults: same; CFTR modulators (e.g., Ivacaftor) weight-based dosing.

brief description: A general term for a decline in mental ability severe enough to interfere with daily life.
causes: Alzheimer's disease, vascular issues, Lewy body disease, and frontotemporal disorders.
symptoms: Memory loss, difficulty thinking, problem-solving, language, and personality changes.
treatment: Cholinesterase inhibitors, memantine, and behavioral interventions.
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: Donepezil 5-10mg once daily; Memantine 5-20mg once/twice daily.

brief description: A buildup of earwax in the ear canal.
causes: Overproduction of earwax, use of cotton swabs, and narrow ear canals.
symptoms: Earache, feeling of fullness in the ear, tinnitus, hearing loss, and dizziness.
treatment: Ear drops to soften wax, irrigation, or manual removal by a healthcare professional.
dosage: Children: Mineral oil drops 1-2 drops twice daily. Adults: Carbamide peroxide drops (6.5%) 5-10 drops twice daily.

brief description: An illness caused by eating contaminated food.
causes: Bacteria (Salmonella, E. coli), viruses, parasites, or toxins in food.
symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, abdominal pain/cramps, and dehydration.
treatment: Hydration (oral rehydration), rest, and sometimes antibiotics or anti-diarrheal medications.
dosage: Children: Oral rehydration solution (ORS) 50-100ml/kg over 4 hours. Adults: ORS as needed; anti-diarrheal Loperamide 4mg initially.

brief description: Inflammation, irritation, or erosion of the protective lining of the stomach.
causes: H. pylori infection, NSAIDs, and excessive alcohol use.
symptoms: Burning or gnawing pain in the upper abdomen, nausea, vomiting, and feeling full after eating.
treatment: Antacids, PPIs, and H2 blockers to reduce stomach acid.
dosage: Children: Omeprazole (0.7-1.4mg/kg) once daily. Adults: Omeprazole (20-40mg) once daily.

brief description: A mild form of gum disease that causes irritation and swelling of the gums.
causes: Plaque buildup on teeth.
symptoms: Swollen, tender gums; gums that bleed easily; bad breath; and receding gums.
treatment: Professional cleaning (scale and polish), improved oral hygiene (brushing and flossing).
dosage: Children: Not applicable. Adults: Not applicable.

brief description: A common type of headache characterized by dull, aching head pain.
causes: Stress, muscle tension, poor posture, and eye strain.
symptoms: Dull, aching pain on both sides of head, pressure behind eyes, and neck/back muscle tension.
treatment: Over-the-counter pain relievers, stress management, and proper ergonomics.
dosage: Children: Paracetamol (10-15mg/kg) every 4-6 hours. Adults: Ibuprofen 200-400mg every 6-8 hours; Acetaminophen 500mg every 4-6 hours.

brief description: A liver infection caused by the hepatitis C virus (HCV).
causes: Contact with infected blood (needle sharing, unscreened blood transfusions).
symptoms: Often asymptomatic initially; later: jaundice, dark urine, fatigue, nausea, and abdominal pain.
treatment: Antiviral medications (Direct-acting antivirals) can cure most infections.
dosage: Children: Direct-acting antivirals (e.g., Sofosbuvir) weight-based for ages 3+. Adults: Epclusa (Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir) 400mg/100mg once daily for 12 weeks.

brief description: A common viral infection causing small, fluid-filled blisters on the lips, mouth, or genitals.
causes: Herpes simplex virus type 1 (oral) or type 2 (genital).
symptoms: Tingling, burning, small blisters, and painful sores.
treatment: Antiviral creams or oral medications (Acyclovir) to shorten outbreaks.
dosage: Children: Oral Acyclovir (15mg/kg) 5 times daily for 5 days. Adults: Oral Acyclovir (400mg) 3 times daily for 5-7 days.

brief description: A condition in which your blood sugar (glucose) level is lower than normal.
causes: Diabetes medications, excessive alcohol, severe liver disease, and hormone deficiencies.
symptoms: Shakiness, dizziness, sweating, hunger, headache, and confusion.
treatment: Consuming fast-acting glucose (juice, candy) and eating a meal/snack soon after.
